reference_law.definition: Finite empirical distribution over all compatible complete cached source records before retained-prompt selection. Each record has mass 1/N; exact duplicate atoms aggregate to pi_j=n_j/N.
reference_law.alternative: Validated explicit finite-law manifest weights remain authoritative; masses of exact duplicate atoms are summed
reference_law.mean: mu_K=sum_j pi_j*u_j; never a model-output center
reference_law.scope: Available-cache empirical distribution, not identification of the checkpoint full training marginal or its sample frequencies
reference_law.single_target_condition: Equation 6 is an assumed experimental idealization; conflicting exact prompt/target records are retained and audited

theory_comparison_mean.definition: Full-vector mean of 10000 unconditional posterior clean references at the minimum SNR of the prespecified analytical extension on independent Gaussian inputs; no network evaluation
theory_comparison_mean.scope: Finite-selected-SNR Monte Carlo estimate, recorded separately from the exact finite-bank mean; sampling uncertainty and measured bank-to-selected offset remain explicit
theory_comparison_mean.prior_dependency: Estimated on the same source-record-weighted posterior law; its immutable cache identity changes with the law.

reference_law.source_unit: One unique complete cached source-record ID, independent of evaluation-seed count or repeated listing. Distinct source IDs with identical atoms contribute separate masses.

reference_law.prior_migration: New law identity requires --recompute-experiments for posterior means/probabilities, reference errors, directional integrals and dependent margins/bounds.
